skills.name: Credit creation: a simplified expansion model and its limits

note.text: A traditional classroom model assumes an outside reserve injection becomes a deposit; banks retain a fixed fraction, lend the remainder and recipients redeposit it completely. With no leakages or excess reserves, the geometric deposit total is the initial deposit divided by the retained fraction. Additional model credit excludes the initial deposit. This is a stylised accounting model, not a mechanical description or prediction of real bank lending. Actual banks create deposits when lending and face demand, risk, capital, liquidity and monetary-policy conditions.

sections.heading: Your goal and connections
sections.text: By the end, you should be able to calculate a model deposit total and separate its assumptions from real bank lending. Builds on: paired loan/deposit entries and bank risk. Leads to: guided model comparison in a Cameroon setting.

sections.heading: Reason and check
sections.text: State the assumptions, convert the percentage to a fraction and identify whether total deposits or additional credit is requested. Do not confuse a limiting total with the result after a few rounds. Explain why actual credit cannot be predicted from this formula alone.

questions.prompt: Stylised closed banking model only: an outside reserve injection of {D} CFA francs becomes an initial deposit. Banks retain fraction {r}/{100} of every deposit; all remainder is lent and redeposited, with no cash leakage or excess reserves. What is the limiting total of deposits, including the initial deposit?

misconceptions.explain: That is additional model credit, excluding the initial deposit; the question asks total deposits.
That is the first-round retained reserve, not the limiting deposit total.

solution: This is an assumed geometric expansion, not a forecast of real lending.
Total deposits = initial deposit / reserve fraction = {D} / ({r}/{100}) = {answer} CFA francs.
Additional model credit excludes the initial deposit: {D*100/r-D}.
